newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures post records, end up.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures post records, end up.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher in a session that saw new record highs for several indices.
June Standard and Poor's 500, technology-laden Nasdaq 100, and small cap Russell 2000, among others, climbed again into record territory.
Trade much of the afternoon was quiet, however, and the strong tone was tied to technology sector strength and a general lack of sellers rather than outright bullishness, traders said.
One trader at a Japanese firm here said the record highs in technology and small-cap indices show a broadening of the stock rally that has fueled record gains in the Dow Jones Industrials.
"I think we're seeing a broadening of the move up," the trader said.
He said traders have now targeted 7,500 in the Dow, but added that Nasdaq could outperform the Dow for the time being.
"The Dow is not the leader here," he said. "It's the Nasdaq." June Nasdaq 100 futures roared above the old record set last week at 966.00 to hit 991.00.
One trader at a U.S. brokerage said June S&P 500 futures action came in spurts, with overall trade quiet on the day.
"There's not much going on," he said. "Sellers have been relatively absent, and dealers when they have been buyers have been coming in real strong," he said.
Chicago Mercantile Exchange price boards showed June S&P 500 futures volume of 79,000 contracts.
Stock index futures had begun the day in lower territory, in step with sagging Treasury bond futures. June T-bonds remained sharply lower all session, despite stock gains.
T-bond futures and June S&Ps downticked after an early batch of U.S. data, and June S&Ps soon shake off the weakness.
The Conference Board reported consumer confidence in May at 127.1 versus 118.5 in April. U.S. April existing home sales fell 2.4 percent to an annual rate of 4.06 million units.

At the close, June S&Ps were up 3.60 points at 851.35, NYSE Composites were up 1.00 at 441.50, KCBT Value Lines were up 2.35 at 751.40, Nikkeis were down 205 at 19,895, Midcap 400s were up 0.35 at 276.80, and Russell 2000s were down 1.15 at 377.35. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
